cells.title: Accept a batch of new cells after a plan revision
cells.action: Per D1 (issue 127). In verbs/state_group/plan_packets.rs `check_batch_matches_approved_preview` refuses with `addCells: batch contains N cell(s), but approved gate preview packet declared M cell(s).` whenever the batch length differs from the whole approved packet (`if cells.len() != approved_cells.len() {`). After a plan revision the packet holds old cells already in the store plus new ones, so a batch of only the new cells is refused while the same cells one by one pass. Replace the length check: keep the per-cell `check_cell_matches_approved_preview` loop, and refuse only when an approved packet cell is neither in the batch nor already a stored cell of the feature (read stored cell ids with the same cells-store reader the module or handlers_write.rs already uses; never a second parser). Name the missing ids in the refusal. Red first in the plan_packets.rs test module (see `pihp_gate_packet_refuses_zero_cells_and_preserves_one_and_seven_cells`): a packet of 3 cells where 1 is already stored and a batch of the other 2 is accepted; a batch that omits an unstored packet cell is refused naming it; an extra undeclared cell is still refused. Keep `pihp_gate_packet_cells_add_refuses_packet_differing_from_approved_preview` in verbs/cells/tests.rs green. No code comments. cells.title: Unwind a refused claim's lease under the session that holds it
cells.action: Per D2 (issue 125). Reported: `bee cells claim --id ruv-1 --worker ruv-code` from main, no --session-id, left the cell status open with no trace.worker while `cells show` reports the claim verdict held, and `dispatch prepare` then refuses claim_ownership not_claimed. Traced cause: `claim_cell_cross_session_ex` (verbs/cells/handlers_write.rs) writes the lease with `claim_cell_file` (verbs/cells/claims.rs), which may adopt a session (`resolve_session_adopt`) when none is given, so the claim file records that adopted session; every later refusal before `write_cell` unwinds with `release_claim(control, session, &cell_id)` using the caller's own session (None), and `release_claim_typed` refuses NOT_OWNER (`if owner.as_deref() != session {`) and the result is discarded, so the lease outlives the refused claim. The reporter saw only the test-results warning and no refusal line, so also check the silent `Err(Fail::Delegate)` unwind near the end of claim_cell_cross_session_ex (it uses the same caller session), and check that the status write (`write_cell`) targets the same store `cells show` and `dispatch prepare` read when the claim runs from main on a cell added from a granted worktree. Fix (smallest shape): right after `ClaimFileOutcome::Ok { claim }` in claim_cell_cross_session_ex, shadow `session` with the session the claim recorded (an owned Option<String>), so every later unwind, `trace.claim_session` and the route-count read use it; do not edit verbs/cells/claims.rs (record in the report that trace.claim_session now carries the adopted session). Red first in verbs/cells/tests.rs: reproduce the torn state — a claim with no session id whose lease gets an adopted session and that then refuses or delegates after the lease (rg -n release_claim verbs/cells/handlers_write.rs) — assert the claim file is gone and a later claim succeeds; watch it fail before the fix. Add a test that a claim without --session-id that succeeds sets status claimed and trace.worker (name it with `claim_without_session`). If you cannot reproduce the reported state, report [BLOCKED] with what you tried instead of guessing. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

truths: a claim that refuses after writing its lease leaves no lease behind, also when the lease adopted a session
a claim without --session-id that succeeds sets status claimed and trace.worker

artifacts.substantive: torn-claim unwind test that failed before the fix

key_links: post-lease unwinds release under the claim file's recorded session
prohibitions: No change to the ownership guard for a different live session

cells.title: Count a directory entry as touched in leader-check
cells.action: Per D3 (issue 121). In verbs/cells/leader_check.rs the commit-diff arm of `run_leader_check` builds `untouched` with `.filter(|f| !paths.contains(f))`, an exact match against the files `git show --name-only` lists, so a files_changed entry that is a directory (`public/chinh-sach`) is refused even when the commit changed files under it. cells.title: Compare canonical paths on Windows for paseo projects and the job mailbox
cells.action: Per D4 (issue 96, Windows CI run 39895071304). Two Windows-only failures. (a) `herding::paseo::tests::ensure_workspace_creates_with_the_main_checkout_project` (herding/paseo.rs ~1748): `rows_with_path` calls `crate::path_identity::canonical_paths_equal`, whose string fallback (`sa.to_lowercase() == sb.to_lowercase()` in path_identity.rs) compares `std::path::absolute` outputs, so a `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...` 8.3 spelling, a `\\?\` prefix or mixed `/` and `\` never match and `--project prj_main` is dropped. On Windows only (`#[cfg(windows)]`), before the string fallback, resolve both sides with `dunce::canonicalize` (the crate already depends on dunce; see verbs/worktree/handlers.rs) when they exist, falling back to the current value when canonicalize fails, and normalize separators; the unix path of canonical_paths_equal must not change (no new symlink resolution on Linux). cells.title: Spend the release permit only after the cheap checks pass
cells.action: Per D6 (issue 117). In scripts/release.sh the line `"$BEE_BIN" dispatch authorize --id "$BEE_DISPATCH_ID" --release-version "$AUTH_VERSION"` (section 2, preconditions) spends a one-time permit before the branch check, the version checks, the tag checks and the release-dirt.sh dirt check of section 3, so any of those refusals burns the permit. Keep the BEE_DISPATCH_ID-set and BEE_BIN-executable checks where they are, and move the authorization so it runs after the zero-mutation refusals and before the first write, on ALL THREE paths the script has: (1) the fresh-release path (`elif [ -n "$ARG_VERSION" ]`): authorize after its first `release-dirt.sh` collection and the remaining zero-mutation checks, right before the version bump; (2) the idempotent re-run path (`ARG_VERSION == HEAD_VERSION`): authorize before its tail; (3) the no-version-argument path, which skips section 3 and goes straight to tag and push: authorize before any tag or push. A simple shape: one shell function `authorize_release` called once per path, with a guard so it never runs twice. No path may reach a write, a tag or a push without a successful authorize. In scripts/release-dirt.sh `is_allowlisted` add `.bee/supervisor/broker-heartbeat.json` (exact path, not a glob). Red first in verbs/drivers/tests.rs: extend `test_release_dirt_script_filters_only_bee_paths` so the heartbeat path is filtered; add a test named `test_release_sh_authorizes_after_cheap_checks_on_every_path` that reads scripts/release.sh and asserts: the first authorize call comes after the first `release-dirt.sh` collection (the one at the fresh-path dirt check, not the ones inside `restore_tree`) and before the bump; and every path that can reach `git tag` or `git push` passes an authorize call first (follow the style of existing release.sh text tests: rg -n release.sh verbs/drivers/tests.rs). Keep `bash -n scripts/release.sh` clean. No code comments added to Rust; keep the script's comment style. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

cells.title: Union-merge the append-only bee logs
cells.action: Per D9 (issue 120). Host repos get no merge driver for bee's append-only logs, so when main and a worktree both append to `.bee/decisions.jsonl` at EOF, `bee worktree merge` aborts on a textual conflict. No Rust code writes `.gitattributes` today; onboarding only splices a `.gitignore` block (`render_gitignore_block` / `merge_gitignore_content` / `find_gitignore_markers` in onboard/merge.rs, markers `# BEE:START` / `# BEE:END` and patterns in onboard/templates.rs). Those markers are valid .gitattributes comments, so REUSE `merge_gitignore_content` and `find_gitignore_markers` unchanged for the new file; the new code is a pattern constant in templates.rs with `merge=union` for `.bee/decisions.jsonl`, `.bee/decisions-archive.jsonl`, `.bee/backlog.jsonl`, `.bee/review-candidates.jsonl`, `.bee/deferred-queue.jsonl` and `.bee/wave-ledger.jsonl`, a render function, a plan item and an apply arm that follow the gitignore block's (rg -n gitignore onboard/plan.rs onboard/apply.rs). A managed-ledger or managed-hash key for the block (like the gitignore one in onboard/plan.rs) is in scope; update the tests that pin that key list. Do NOT hand-edit this repo's root `.gitattributes`: this repo gets the block from its own onboarding via `bee dev regen`; record that in the report. cells.title: Refuse a merge up front when main holds untracked history files the branch writes
cells.action: Per D10 (issue 122). Before `git merge --no-ff --no-commit`, `commit_main_bookkeeping` (verbs/worktree/merge.rs) runs `git add -A --` over `main_bookkeeping_roots`, which include `docs/history/<feature>`, and commits them on main. When main holds UNTRACKED copies of history files the branch also adds (e.g. CONTEXT.md, leader-check.json), that commit turns them into main-side additions and the merge meets an add/add conflict, then fails WORKTREE_MERGE_ABORT_FAILED. Git itself refuses a merge over an untracked file the branch writes, for identical and for different bytes alike (leader ran it: `untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge`), so the files cannot be merged over. In `merge_stage` (verbs/worktree/phases.rs) the untracked-collision check (`main_dirt_excluding(main_root, &roots)` and the `blocking_untracked` list that becomes WORKTREE_MERGE_MAIN_DIRTY) skips everything under the bookkeeping roots. Extend it: untracked paths under the bookkeeping roots that the merging branch also writes (reuse the existing branch-changed-files helper; rg -n branch_changed_files verbs/worktree/) join `blocking_untracked`, so the merge refuses up front, zero mutations, with the existing WORKTREE_MERGE_MAIN_DIRTY refusal naming them — before `commit_main_bookkeeping` runs. Also make `commit_main_bookkeeping` (merge.rs) never stage those paths (pass the exclusions in, or filter specs), as a second fence. If a code comment in phases.rs says no untracked path is ever swept, delete it because it is now false; add no comments. Red first in verbs/worktree/tests.rs next to `an_untracked_path_the_branch_does_write_still_refuses_and_is_named`: main holds an untracked `docs/history/<feature>/CONTEXT.md` that the branch also adds; assert the merge refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_MAIN_DIRTY naming that path, main's HEAD did not move, and `git status --porcelain` on main shows no staged entry; watch it fail first (today it ends WORKTREE_MERGE_ABORT_FAILED or a conflict). Keep `a_failing_bookkeeping_commit_only_warns_and_the_merge_still_completes_green` and the untracked-collision pair green. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

truths: an untracked docs/history/<feature> file on main that the branch writes makes the merge refuse WORKTREE_MERGE_MAIN_DIRTY naming it, with zero mutations
the bookkeeping commit never stages such a file
key_links: merge_stage adds branch-written untracked bookkeeping paths to blocking_untracked
prohibitions: No deletion of user files on main

cells.title: Unwind a refused claim's lease under the session that holds it
cells.action: Per D2 (issue 125). Reported: `bee cells claim --id ruv-1 --worker ruv-code` from main, no --session-id, left the cell status open with no trace.worker while `cells show` reports the claim verdict held, and `dispatch prepare` then refuses claim_ownership not_claimed. Traced cause: `claim_cell_cross_session_ex` (verbs/cells/handlers_write.rs) writes the lease with `claim_cell_file` (verbs/cells/claims.rs), which may adopt a session (`resolve_session_adopt`) when none is given, so the claim file records that adopted session; every later refusal before `write_cell` unwinds with `release_claim(control, session, &cell_id)` using the caller's own session (None), and `release_claim_typed` refuses NOT_OWNER (`if owner.as_deref() != session {`) and the result is discarded, so the lease outlives the refused claim. The reporter saw only the test-results warning and no refusal line, so also check the silent `Err(Fail::Delegate)` unwind near the end of claim_cell_cross_session_ex (it uses the same caller session), and check that the status write (`write_cell`) targets the same store `cells show` and `dispatch prepare` read when the claim runs from main on a cell added from a granted worktree. Fix (smallest shape): right after `ClaimFileOutcome::Ok { claim }` in claim_cell_cross_session_ex, shadow `session` with the session the claim recorded (an owned Option<String>), so every later unwind, `trace.claim_session` and the route-count read use it; do not edit verbs/cells/claims.rs (record in the report that trace.claim_session now carries the adopted session). Red first in verbs/cells/tests.rs: reproduce the torn state — a claim with no session id whose lease gets an adopted session and that then refuses or delegates after the lease (rg -n release_claim verbs/cells/handlers_write.rs) — assert the claim file is gone and a later claim succeeds; watch it fail before the fix. Add a test that a claim without --session-id that succeeds sets status claimed and trace.worker (name it with `claim_without_session`). If you cannot reproduce the reported state, report [BLOCKED] with what you tried instead of guessing. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

truths: a claim that refuses after writing its lease leaves no lease behind, also when the lease adopted a session
a claim without --session-id that succeeds sets status claimed and trace.worker

artifacts.substantive: torn-claim unwind test that failed before the fix

key_links: post-lease unwinds release under the claim file's recorded session
prohibitions: No change to the ownership guard for a different live session

cells.title: Count a directory entry as touched in leader-check
cells.action: Per D3 (issue 121). In verbs/cells/leader_check.rs the commit-diff arm of `run_leader_check` builds `untouched` with `.filter(|f| !paths.contains(f))`, an exact match against the files `git show --name-only` lists, so a files_changed entry that is a directory (`public/chinh-sach`) is refused even when the commit changed files under it. Treat an entry as touched when a committed path equals it or starts with the entry plus `/` (after `normalize_cell_path`; strip one trailing `/` from the entry first). Red first in the leader_check.rs test module next to `claimed_file_in_trailer_commit_passes_with_commit_diff_checked`: a commit that touches `d/a.txt` and `d/sub/b.txt` with files_changed `["d"]` passes; `["dx"]` with a commit touching `d/a.txt` is still refused naming `dx`. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

truths: a directory entry in files_changed passes when the commit touched a file under it
a path that is only a string prefix of a touched path is still refused
key_links: the untouched filter uses a component prefix match
prohibitions: No change to the trailer-commit lookup

cells.title: Tell a dead claim-gate pid on Windows
cells.action: Per D4 (issue 96, Windows CI run 39895071304). `fn gate_pid_dead` in verbs/cells/claims.rs returns false on every non-unix target (`#[cfg(not(unix))]` arm), so on Windows the test `verbs::cells::tests::unclaim_breaks_a_dead_pid_gate_that_is_younger_than_the_age_window` fails: a fresh gate with pid 999999999 reads live and the unclaim keeps the claim. `crate::lock::is_pid_alive` (lock.rs) already has a Windows arm (OpenProcess with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER); reuse it — no new unsafe code and no second copy of the liveness logic. Replace the `#[cfg(not(unix))]` arm body with a `#[cfg(windows)]` arm that returns the negation of that helper for the pid (adapt the argument type to its signature), and keep a `#[cfg(not(any(unix, windows)))]` arm returning false. The unix arm does not change. Proof: Linux `cargo test claims` stays green and `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` (if the target is installed; else record that it was skipped) compiles; the Windows CI after merge is the live proof — say so in the report. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

truths: on Windows gate_pid_dead reports a non-existent pid as dead
on Windows a live pid is never reported dead
unix behaviour is unchanged

cells.title: Compare canonical paths on Windows for paseo projects and the job mailbox
cells.action: Per D4 (issue 96, Windows CI run 39895071304). Two Windows-only failures. (a) `herding::paseo::tests::ensure_workspace_creates_with_the_main_checkout_project` (herding/paseo.rs ~1748): `rows_with_path` calls `crate::path_identity::canonical_paths_equal`, whose string fallback (`sa.to_lowercase() == sb.to_lowercase()` in path_identity.rs) compares `std::path::absolute` outputs, so a `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...` 8.3 spelling, a `\\?\` prefix or mixed `/` and `\` never match and `--project prj_main` is dropped. On Windows only (`#[cfg(windows)]`), before the string fallback, resolve both sides with `dunce::canonicalize` (the crate already depends on dunce; see verbs/worktree/handlers.rs) when they exist, falling back to the current value when canonicalize fails, and normalize separators; the unix path of canonical_paths_equal must not change (no new symlink resolution on Linux). (b) `hooks::worker_guard::tests::read_only_table` (hooks/worker_guard.rs ~519-547): `in_mailbox` compares `settle(&absolute)` with `settle(mailbox)` by `starts_with`; `settle` uses `std::fs::canonicalize` (verbatim `\\?\` paths on Windows) and the test target mixes `\` with `/`, so `mv <mailbox>/result-1.json.tmp <mailbox>/result-1.json` is denied. Make `settle` use `dunce::canonicalize` (on unix it equals std canonicalize, so Linux results do not change) and push the lexical components so separators are uniform on both sides. Do not change herding/paseo.rs. Proof: Linux tests for both modules stay green (`cargo test path_identity`, `cargo test worker_guard`); the Windows CI after merge is the live proof — say so in the report. No code comments. cells.title: Spend the release permit only after the cheap checks pass
cells.action: Per D6 (issue 117). In scripts/release.sh the line `"$BEE_BIN" dispatch authorize --id "$BEE_DISPATCH_ID" --release-version "$AUTH_VERSION"` (section 2, preconditions) spends a one-time permit before the branch check, the version checks, the tag checks and the release-dirt.sh dirt check of section 3, so any of those refusals burns the permit. Keep the BEE_DISPATCH_ID-set and BEE_BIN-executable checks where they are, and move the authorization so it runs after the zero-mutation refusals and before the first write, on ALL THREE paths the script has: (1) the fresh-release path (`elif [ -n "$ARG_VERSION" ]`): authorize after its first `release-dirt.sh` collection and the remaining zero-mutation checks, right before the version bump; (2) the idempotent re-run path (`ARG_VERSION == HEAD_VERSION`): authorize before its tail; (3) the no-version-argument path, which skips section 3 and goes straight to tag and push: authorize before any tag or push. A simple shape: one shell function `authorize_release` called once per path, with a guard so it never runs twice. No path may reach a write, a tag or a push without a successful authorize. In scripts/release-dirt.sh `is_allowlisted` add `.bee/supervisor/broker-heartbeat.json` (exact path, not a glob). Red first in verbs/drivers/tests.rs: extend `test_release_dirt_script_filters_only_bee_paths` so the heartbeat path is filtered; add a test named `test_release_sh_authorizes_after_cheap_checks_on_every_path` that reads scripts/release.sh and asserts: the first authorize call comes after the first `release-dirt.sh` collection (the one at the fresh-path dirt check, not the ones inside `restore_tree`) and before the bump; and every path that can reach `git tag` or `git push` passes an authorize call first (follow the style of existing release.sh text tests: rg -n release.sh verbs/drivers/tests.rs). Keep `bash -n scripts/release.sh` clean. No code comments added to Rust; keep the script's comment style. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.
cells.verify: bash -n scripts/release.sh && PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee release

the re-run path and the no-version path still authorize before any tag or push
release-dirt.sh does not list .bee/supervisor/broker-heartbeat.json
key_links: the order test reads scripts/release.sh
prohibitions: No change to what the release commit carries

cells.title: Stop the Paseo agent when the ceiling times out
cells.action: Per D7 (issue 123). In herding/run.rs both paseo `PollDecision::TimedOutCeiling` arms (first round in `execute_paseo`, and the `--continue` round loop) only print `paseo worker hit the ceiling; pane kept for inspection` and return RunOutcome::TimedOutCeiling, so the Paseo agent keeps running and writing after the job returns. cells.title: Union-merge the append-only bee logs
cells.action: Per D9 (issue 120). Host repos get no merge driver for bee's append-only logs, so when main and a worktree both append to `.bee/decisions.jsonl` at EOF, `bee worktree merge` aborts on a textual conflict. No Rust code writes `.gitattributes` today; onboarding only splices a `.gitignore` block (`render_gitignore_block` / `merge_gitignore_content` / `find_gitignore_markers` in onboard/merge.rs, markers `# BEE:START` / `# BEE:END` and patterns in onboard/templates.rs). Those markers are valid .gitattributes comments, so REUSE `merge_gitignore_content` and `find_gitignore_markers` unchanged for the new file; the new code is a pattern constant in templates.rs with `merge=union` for `.bee/decisions.jsonl`, `.bee/decisions-archive.jsonl`, `.bee/backlog.jsonl`, `.bee/review-candidates.jsonl`, `.bee/deferred-queue.jsonl` and `.bee/wave-ledger.jsonl`, a render function, a plan item and an apply arm that follow the gitignore block's (rg -n gitignore onboard/plan.rs onboard/apply.rs). A managed-ledger or managed-hash key for the block (like the gitignore one in onboard/plan.rs) is in scope; update the tests that pin that key list. Do NOT hand-edit this repo's root `.gitattributes`: this repo gets the block from its own onboarding via `bee dev regen`; record that in the report. Red first in onboard/tests.rs next to the gitignore block tests: onboarding a fresh repo writes the block; re-running is a no-op; host lines outside the markers survive; and a real git test — two branches that each append one line to `.bee/decisions.jsonl` after onboarding merge without conflict (follow the git-fixture style already in onboard/tests.rs or verbs/worktree/tests.rs). If the release-manifest check or regen chain names a new obligation, run it and record it. No code comments. a re-run changes nothing and host lines outside the block survive

cells.title: Refuse a merge up front when main holds untracked history files the branch writes
cells.action: Per D10 (issue 122). Before `git merge --no-ff --no-commit`, `commit_main_bookkeeping` (verbs/worktree/merge.rs) runs `git add -A --` over `main_bookkeeping_roots`, which include `docs/history/<feature>`, and commits them on main. When main holds UNTRACKED copies of history files the branch also adds (e.g. CONTEXT.md, leader-check.json), that commit turns them into main-side additions and the merge meets an add/add conflict, then fails WORKTREE_MERGE_ABORT_FAILED. Git itself refuses a merge over an untracked file the branch writes, for identical and for different bytes alike (leader ran it: `untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge`), so the files cannot be merged over. In `merge_stage` (verbs/worktree/phases.rs) the untracked-collision check (`main_dirt_excluding(main_root, &roots)` and the `blocking_untracked` list that becomes WORKTREE_MERGE_MAIN_DIRTY) skips everything under the bookkeeping roots. Extend it: untracked paths under the bookkeeping roots that the merging branch also writes (reuse the existing branch-changed-files helper; rg -n branch_changed_files verbs/worktree/) join `blocking_untracked`, so the merge refuses up front, zero mutations, with the existing WORKTREE_MERGE_MAIN_DIRTY refusal naming them — before `commit_main_bookkeeping` runs. Also make `commit_main_bookkeeping` (merge.rs) never stage those paths (pass the exclusions in, or filter specs), as a second fence. If a code comment in phases.rs says no untracked path is ever swept, delete it because it is now false; add no comments. Red first in verbs/worktree/tests.rs next to `an_untracked_path_the_branch_does_write_still_refuses_and_is_named`: main holds an untracked `docs/history/<feature>/CONTEXT.md` that the branch also adds; assert the merge refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_MAIN_DIRTY naming that path, main's HEAD did not move, and `git status --porcelain` on main shows no staged entry; watch it fail first (today it ends WORKTREE_MERGE_ABORT_FAILED or a conflict). Keep `a_failing_bookkeeping_commit_only_warns_and_the_merge_still_completes_green` and the untracked-collision pair green. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

truths: an untracked docs/history/<feature> file on main that the branch writes makes the merge refuse WORKTREE_MERGE_MAIN_DIRTY naming it, with zero mutations
the bookkeeping commit never stages such a file
key_links: merge_stage adds branch-written untracked bookkeeping paths to blocking_untracked
prohibitions: No deletion of user files on main

cells.title: Let route --set name its lane record
cells.action: Per D11 (issue 124). `run_route` in verbs/state_group/workflows.rs passes `None` as the lane record to `resolve_mutation_lock_scope` and `resolve_mutation_target(&ctx.root, None, "route", no_lane)`, so an unbound session can only write the bound lane or the default record and is refused while lanes are live. Its `--lane` flag is the triage lane classification (ROUTE_LANE_VALUES), so it cannot be the selector. Add `--lane-record <feature>` through the SAME selector the other verbs use (D11): `mutation_lane_selector` in verbs/state_group/flags.rs hard-reads the `lane` key, so give it (or a thin sibling that both share) a flag-key parameter, keep every existing caller on `lane`, and have run_route call it with `lane-record`; pass the result as the lane to both resolvers (refuses a missing or corrupt lane; refuses together with --no-lane); add it to keys_known; mention it in the unbound refusal's FIX text. `bee route` and `bee state route` are two registry entries over the same run_route: declare the flag on BOTH in generated/registry_payload.json by hand (follow an existing flag entry there; catalog.rs reads REGISTRY_PAYLOAD), and bump `PINNED_FLAG_COUNT` in catalog.rs by one (231 at plan time — read the current value) with a reason line in the same style as earlier bumps (that pin reason is the one comment this cell may add). Red first in tests/route_lane_targeting.rs next to `an_unbound_set_against_the_default_record_is_refused_while_lanes_are_live`: an unbound `state route --set ... --lane-record <f>` writes the route into that lane record and leaves the default record untouched, and the same through `bee route --set ... --lane-record <f>`; `--lane-record` with `--no-lane` refuses; an unknown lane refuses. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.
